# Inside the Xiuhtēcuhtli restoration: what the marks recover
The domain you're reading about exists because someone refused to let **Xiuhtēcuhtli** stay *xiuhtecuhtli*.

Xiuhtēcuhtli's myths are the calendar's: the fire that must be renewed, and the darkness that waits if it is not. At the close of each 52-year cycle (xiuhmolpilli), the Aztec world extinguished every flame: households went dark, debts were settled, and the priests climbed Huixachtlan — Hill of the Star — to watch for the Pleiades' midnight passage.  On a captive's chest the fire-priest drilled the new flame; if it caught, the runner carried it to the Templo Mayor, and every hearth in the empire was relit from it.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Xiuhtēcuhtli
- **ASCII form:** xiuhtecuhtli
- **Meaning:** ""Fire Lord" — the Aztec fire god, lord of the hearth and of the year"
- **Domain of influence:** Fire, Time, Hearth
- **Pantheon:** Nahuatl
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** —
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 265 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

**Xiuhtēcuhtli** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *xiuhtecuhtli* and **Xiuhtēcuhtli** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Xiuhtēcuhtli** lives at [/sites/xiuhtecuhtli/](/sites/xiuhtecuhtli/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/xiuhtecuhtli/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/xiuhtecuhtli/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/xiuhtecuhtli/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Xiuhtēcuhtli** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Timekeeping & Calendar Systems** — The 52-year New Fire cycle; time restarted by hand.
- **Thermal, Geothermal & Fire Energy** — The Aztec fire itself — first and last of the gods, the hearth at the center of the universe; heat made lord.
- **Manufacturing, Craft & Automation** — The fire-drill and the forge; the hearth of all making.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
